 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Sunday-morning coffee in Atlanta comes with a 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff from Spain, and the Falcons' best player is the one asking the most of himself. Bijan Robinson leads the NFL with 780 rushing yards, yet he spent part of the week explaining why that number doesn't satisfy him before the Cincinnati Bengals game at the Santiago Bernabéu.
 "I'll be honest, I don't feel like I'm playing like that right now," Robinson said, according to TSN . "I got to be better. I got to be better for this team." He hasn't run for a touchdown since a 59-yard score at New Orleans on Oct. 5, and he ran 19 times for 76 yards in last week's 16-0 loss in Tampa .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement What to expect from Bijan Robinson against Cincinnati
 Oct 18, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson (7) is tackled by Chicago Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson (48) during the first quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images
 1. A workload north of 20 touches 
 Brian Robinson Jr. is out again with a hamstring injury, which leaves Khalil Herbert as the only other back with carries this season. Bijan Robinson had 20 carries against San Francisco and 19 at Tampa Bay in the two games Brian Robinson Jr. missed, and he was targeted on top of that. Expect Kevin Stefanski to lean on him early, because a bigger problem than their quarterback has been Atlanta's inability to stay on schedule.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement 2. At least one run that breaks loose 
 Pull up the splits since Oct. 5 and Robinson has 286 yards on 65 carries over his last four games, 4.4 per carry, after piling up 494 yards on 85 carries (5.8) in his first four. Cincinnati's defense allows 4.8 yards per carry, per ESPN's team stats . That defense also allows the fifth-lowest rushing success rate in the league, according to Bengals.com's scouting report , so the yards are coming in chunks rather than steady gains.
 Robinson has eight runs of 20 or more yards and has forced 44 missed tackles, third among running backs, per that same report. The Bengals missed eight tackles against Tennessee last week, according to PFF, in a game in which they gave up 440 yards .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement 3. More work in the passing game 
 Michael Penix Jr. gets rid of the ball in 2.59 seconds on average, second-fastest in the NFL by Bengals.com's count, and Robinson has 25 catches for 203 yards. Cincinnati linebacker Barrett Carter leads the team with 58 tackles but allowed 49 yards on two catches against the Titans, according to PFF, and Demetrius Knight Jr. allowed all four passes thrown his way.
 Check-downs that get Robinson in space against those two linebackers are a cleaner path than pounding into Dexter Lawrence, who had five defensive stops last week. After four interceptions in Tampa, Penix needs the easy completions, too, as we covered in looking for his breakout game .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement 4. The goal-line carries are his 
 Brian Robinson Jr. has four rushing touchdowns this season, the same as Bijan. With him out, the short-yardage work near the end zone belongs to Robinson, and that's the most direct route to ending the drought. Cincinnati has allowed 22.6 points per game, and Atlanta can't afford to settle for field goals against an offense averaging 29.4.
 Robinson called this a "playoff-type game" for a 3-5 team sitting within a half-game of first place in the NFC South, a race we broke down in who has the edge this week . If the Falcons are going to keep pace with Joe Burrow, it starts with Robinson looking like the back who ran for 194 yards in Green Bay in September.
